title: Introduce throughput stitcher and phase-aware decline detector
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add throughput stitching aggregator and new phase-aware decline detector; default guard enabled behind flag; dashboards updated; rollout policy extended to require two-sensor corroboration for automatic cutovers.
body:
Title: Introduce throughput stitcher and phase-aware decline detector

Description: This PR adds a new component, the 'throughput stitcher', to consolidate fine-grained throughput samples across rolling micro-phases into coherent windows, and a complementary 'phase-aware decline detector' that identifies gradual throughput degradation that would otherwise be masked by natural traffic oscillations. The goal is to catch slow, progressive regressions (e.g., warmup/steady-state drift, memory pressure tails) before they affect customer SLAs and to provide a conservative rollout guard that prevents automatic cutovers on marginal signals.

Motivation and context:
- We observe recurring incidents where throughput drops slowly over hours (0.5-5% sustained) and escape the existing canary because per-window volatility and traffic phase changes (spiky/bursty user load) mask the drift.
- Current detectors are tuned for abrupt regressions (change-points) or tail latency spikes, but long-tail throughput decay is a distinct failure mode requiring a different signal fusion approach.
- Related tickets: ENG-1342 backlog item for long-run throughput regressions; SUP-234 customer report showing 8-hour slow decay in Dedicated clusters.

What this change does: (single continuous description)
- Introduces throughput-stitcher service (pkg/perf/stitcher): ingests per-probe throughput samples (per-replica, 10s resolution), aligns them by micro-phase markers (probe/burst IDs), and produces stitched windows representing contiguous operational phases. Stitcher outputs both absolute and normalized throughput curves plus a synthetic 'phase-entropy' score that quantifies intra-window shape variability.
- Adds phase-aware-decline detector (pkg/perf/detectors/phase_decline): consumes stitched windows and runs a two-stage analysis: (1) trend extraction with robust local regression + exponential smoothing (tunable half-life), (2) gradual-decline hypothesis test combining a monotonicity score and a Bayesian drift probability. Detector correlates throughput drift with tail-latency and P50/P90 to reduce false positives from benign traffic shifts.
- Rollout guard integration (orchestrator/canary_guard): new guard 'phase_decline_guard' that prevents automated ramp or cutover if the detector reports sustained decline above configured thresholds on two independent sensors (throughput-stitcher + tail-latency cross-check). The guard can be configured to 'warn-only' for early runs.
- Observability: dashboard panels added (grafana/dashboards/throughput_stitched.json) showing stitched windows, phase-entropy, monotonicity score, and Bayesian drift probability. Alerts and a low-volume synthetic probe were added to exercise long-window detection.
- Tests: unit tests for stitcher and detector, integration test that replays recorded traffic traces with known slow decay patterns, and an e2e regression scenario that validates guard behavior under mixed-phase changes.

Commit summary: (high-level)
- a1b2c3d  Add throughput stitcher core, windowing and entropy scoring (pkg/perf/stitcher)
- d4e5f6g  Implement phase-aware decline detector with Bayesian drift engine (pkg/perf/detectors)
- h7i8j9k  Guard integration and canary policy updates (orchestrator/canary_guard.go)
- l0m1n2o  Observability: dashboards + alert rules + README for tuning
- p3q4r5s  Tests: unit + integration + e2e trace replay and CI configs

Files / areas changed (high level list):
- pkg/perf/stitcher/*.go: new aggregator and window encoder (core algorithm ~220 LOC).
- pkg/perf/detectors/phase_decline.go: new detector with configurable parameters.
- orchestrator/canary_guard.go: add guard registration and policy checks.
- grafana/dashboards/throughput_stitched.json: new dashboard panels.
- testdata/traces/decay-replay.jsonl: synthetic long-run decay trace used in integration tests.
- integration/tests/phase_decline_integration_test.go: end-to-end verification harness.
- docs/perf/phase-decline-detector.md: design doc + tuning guidance.

Small illustrative snippet (stitcher high-level behavior):
"""
// pseudo: align samples by phase-id and stitch into window
for each phaseID in incomingPhases {
  window := stitcher.BuildWindow(phaseID)
  window.NormalizeByReplicaCount()
  window.ComputePhaseEntropy()
  emit(window)
}
"""

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for monotonicity scoring and synthetic trace replay.
- CI initially failed on integration test due to flaky event ordering in the replay harness; fixed by adding deterministic seeding and re-running pipeline. Final CI: all checks passing (lint, unit, integration, e2e).

Performance considerations:
- Stitcher keeps in-memory buffers per active phase; memory bounded by configured max-phase-duration and max-replicas. Default limits chosen conservatively to avoid impact on control-plane memory.
- Detector uses incremental smoothing to avoid O(N) re-compute on long windows.

Backward compatibility:
- New guard is behind a feature flag (canary.phase_decline_guard.enabled=false by default). Dashboards are additive. No public API changes.

Review conversation (high level condensed but continuous):
- Diego Martinez (review): "Nice work — the sketch makes sense. Two asks: 1) add a short-run ablation test showing step-change doesn't trigger the decline detector; 2) provide explicit guidance for tuning half-life vs. window size. Also can we make the entropy metric pluggable?"
- Aisha (author): "Thanks Diego — added ablation test (integration/tests/ablation_step_change.go) and expanded docs with tuning appendix. Made entropy strategy an interface and added a default implementation. PTAL."
- Ling Zhao (review): "Can we avoid unbounded maps in stitcher? Also, please add more logging around phase eviction so we can debug long-lived phases."
- Aisha: "Good catch — added eviction policy with soft TTL and metrics for eviction counts. Reduced default max-phase-duration to 6h. Updated tests accordingly."
- Priya Srinivasan (security/ops): "Ensure no sensitive identifiers are emitted to metrics; confirm logs scrub replica IDs."
- Aisha: "Confirmed and added redaction in stitcher logging. Unit test added to validate redaction."

Approval and merge:
- After two review cycles and CI stabilization, reviewers approved. Maintainers requested a squash merge.
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Post-merge action: flip the guard to warn-only in a canary for one week, collect telemetry and tune thresholds before enabling block-mode. A follow-up Linear task ENG-1399 created for rollout tuning and long-term GA.

Notes and rationale for uniqueness:
- This PR focuses on gradual throughput decay (distinct from abrupt canary regressions) and introduces a stitching abstraction to reason about phase boundaries explicitly. The enrollment of a two-sensor corroboration guard is intentionally conservative to reduce false positives during mixed traffic scenarios.

If you want to try it out locally:
1) enable feature flag via env CANARY_PHASE_DECLINE=true in local dev;
2) run integration replay: ./bin/replay -trace testdata/traces/decay-replay.jsonl -target http://localhost:8080;
3) inspect grafana/dashboards/throughput_stitched.json.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current stitching assumes phase IDs are available from synthetic probes; for real traffic we'd need inference heuristics (ENG-1399).
- Detector tuning remains conservative; early canary will run in warn-only mode.
- Future work: add multi-cluster aggregation and cross-region corroboration rules.
